templates.name: Windows Tools (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for the windows_bootstrap/windows_hygiene playbook families -- the Windows equivalent of linuxtools_examplemusic. Built 2026-10-26, same flat/native, one-item-per-thing design as every other template in this series, from a real shopping list (every windows_bootstrap/playbooks/*.yml + shared tasks/*.yml file read in full) plus items ported from a real reference Zabbix template (docs/zabbix_templates/ex1_windows.json, gitignored, never committed).

DESIGN NOTES
- registry.data[]/registry.get[]/service.info[] are real, native Zabbix Windows agent item keys, confirmed directly against the current 7.0 manual before use -- not assumed. Covers almost every registry/service check in this template natively, no shell-out needed.
- Chocolatey package-presence uses the <packageid>.nuspec convention (every installed package ships this NuGet metadata file in its own lib\<pkg>\ folder, regardless of what's inside tools\) -- Robert's own call, UNVERIFIED against a real live box yet, same working-hypothesis treatment as every other first-pass assumption in this series until proven (the Zabbix stock-template-name assumption is the precedent).
- No native Zabbix Windows item exists for firewall rules or Windows optional features/capabilities (confirmed against the real 7.0 docs, not guessed) -- those use system.run[] PowerShell invocations, same category as this series' own Linux system.run[] checks.
- GUI-only Chocolatey packages (choco_packages_gui) and the OpenRSAT.exe substitute are gated via a TRIGGER DEPENDENCY on InstallationType (Client/Server/Server Core), the same real registry signal 40-choco-packages.yml's own has_gui detection already trusts -- Robert's own suggestion, not a second redundant macro.
- VMware Tools is NOT Chocolatey-installed (tasks/guest_tools.yml's own 2026-09-21 finding -- the hypervisor's own mechanism installs it) -- checked via its real binary path instead, macro-gated the same way as qemu-guest-agent.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHECKED THIS ROUND (scoped out, not forgotten)
- HKCU-based screensaver values (SCRNSAVE.EXE, ScreenSaveActive, etc) -- registry.data reads the Zabbix agent SERVICE's own HKCU (SYSTEM's hive), not the real interactive user's, so these aren't reliably checkable this way.
- registry_deadvertise's own per-item list (group_vars/windows_desktop|laptop/, contents not read this round) -- only the one well-known named value (DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures) is checked.
- sacsvr startup-type exact numeric encoding -- only state is checked (visibility only, no trigger, see that item's own description for why).
- RustDesk persistent ID (RustDesk2.toml) -- real equivalent to TeamViewer's ClientID exists, but only reliably at a single path when running as a service; choco_packages_common.yml's own rustdesk.install is a plain install with no service configuration, so the file's location isn't guaranteed yet. Flagged to Robert, not built.
- Salt Minion version extraction -- service presence/running state is checked (service.info), not its installed version (would need registry.get[]'s JSON shape, unconfirmed, or a system.run reg query -- deferred rather than guessed).
- Locale (en-GB) -- split across multiple HKCU-rooted settings, same service-context mismatch risk as the screensaver values above.

ex1_windows.json cross-reference: TeamViewer ID checks (x2) -- NOT applicable, RustDesk is this estate's actual remote-access tool, see the RustDesk note above. clearpageonreboot.cmd checksum/exists -- NOT applicable, a bespoke script from a different real environment; the real registry value it was checking (ClearPageFileAtShutdown) IS checked above. Dual-path Zabbix agent config checks -- not ported, this estate has one single known install path ({$WINDOWSTOOLS.ZABBIX_CONF_PATH}).

items.name: Screen-lock inactivity timeout
items.description: Native registry.data[] read of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs. Expected value: {$WINDOWSTOOLS.LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS}. Compared against {$WINDOWSTOOLS.LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS} (default matches exa_lock_timeout_secs, group_vars/all/vars.yml). Set by tasks/screenlock.yml. NOTE: the companion HKCU screensaver values (SCRNSAVE.EXE etc) are NOT checked here -- registry.data reads the Zabbix agent SERVICE's own HKCU (SYSTEM's hive), not the real interactive user's, so those values aren't reliably checkable this way. Deliberately scoped out, not forgotten.

Ported from ex1_windows.json's own Windows Build Number item (that one used the deprecated wmic path -- this is the real registry value instead).

items.name: Hibernation enabled/disabled matches expectation
items.description: Native registry.data[] read of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\HibernateEnabled. Expected value: {$WINDOWSTOOLS.HIBERNATION_EXPECTED}. Set by powercfg /hibernate on|off (playbooks/70-hibernation.yml, chassis-dependent via exa_hibernation_enabled). Standard real registry value for this -- independently corroborated by docs/management/WindowsHygiene.xml's own (never-confirmed) WMI-based check for the exact same value name. {$WINDOWSTOOLS.HIBERNATION_EXPECTED} holds the numeric DWORD directly (0 or 1), not yes/no -- simpler than a second macro for the same concept, since this is the only item that needs it.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} — Hibernation enabled/disabled matches expectation is not set correctly
triggers.description: Expected {$WINDOWSTOOLS.HIBERNATION_EXPECTED}, see this item's own description for the real registry path.

items.name: Windows installation type (Client/Server/Server Core)
items.description: Native registry.data[] read of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\InstallationType. Visibility only, no trigger. Same real signal windows_bootstrap/playbooks/40-choco-packages.yml's own has_gui detection already trusts ("Client"/"Server"/"Server Core"). Visibility only here, but used by this template's own RSAT/GUI-package trigger dependencies below -- the gating signal Robert asked for, not a separate macro.

items.name: Timezone (TimeZoneKeyName)
items.description: Native registry.data[] read of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\TimeZoneInformation\TimeZoneKeyName. Visibility only, no trigger. Standard Windows registry location tzutil.exe itself uses. Expected "GMT Standard Time" (tasks/locale_timezone.yml). Visibility only for now -- not independently re-tested live this round, flagged as a working assumption, same discipline as every other first-pass item in this series.

items.description: Native service.info[sshd] (state). 0=running, 1=paused, 6=stopped, 255=service does not exist. Expected: running (0).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} — sshd service is not running
triggers.description: Expected state 0 (running).

items.name: TermService (RDP) running
items.description: Native service.info[TermService] (state). 0=running, 1=paused, 6=stopped, 255=service does not exist. Expected: running (0).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} — TermService service is not running
triggers.description: Expected state 0 (running).

items.name: salt-minion service running
items.description: Native service.info[salt-minion] (state). 0=running, 1=paused, 6=stopped, 255=service does not exist. Expected: running (0).

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} — salt-minion service is not running
triggers.description: Expected state 0 (running).

items.name: wuauserv service state
items.description: Native service.info[wuauserv] (state). 0=running, 1=paused, 6=stopped, 255=service does not exist. Expected: running (0). Visibility only, no trigger -- wuauserv is demand-start and legitimately stopped most of the time even when healthy; a 'not running' check would be a guaranteed false positive.

items.name: sacsvr startup configured (Server only)
items.description: Native service.info[sacsvr] (state). 0=running, 1=paused, 6=stopped, 255=service does not exist. Expected: running (0). Visibility only -- sacsvr is auto-start but only actually RUNS after the next reboot (tasks/sac_ems.yml's own 2026-08-14 finding); a 'not running' trigger would false-positive on every box that hasn't rebooted since the BCD settings were applied.
